Four points are placed at the outer corners to maximize boundary constraints. To mitigate the concentration of area in the center (which occurs in naive grid packings), the center point and the midpoints of the edges are radially perturbed toward the subcenters of their respective quadrants. Specifically, points are shifted by 1/8 of the total side length from their expected symmetrical positions to ensure no three points are collinear and all lie exactly on half-integer or quarter-integer fractions. This distributes the minimum triangle areas across the internal lattice intersections, setting the smallest determinant to 1/32 (an area of 1/64 = 0.015625).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
